text:
Alexander Nikishin's season didn't start until November 7. The restricted free agent missed training camp and the first month in a contract standoff with Carolina, with reports (Daily Faceoff, theScore) that he had asked for a trade and that the Hurricanes were open to moving him, before the two sides settled on a one-year deal. He scored in his season debut, a 9-2 win over Chicago, and Yahoo Sports was still asking this week whether Winnipeg might pursue him.

Six games is nowhere near enough to judge, but the start is loud: three goals and five points, on just 0.53 expected goals. Shooting 33% is not a skill anyone keeps, and our talent range has his true scoring rate around 1.4 points per 60, not the 2.93 he's at now.

What's real is the player Carolina had last season, when he helped win the Stanley Cup. Evolving-Hockey had him 36th among 215 defensemen, with most of his value on the power play, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found him stopping 15% of entries at his blue line. His shot is a weapon (96th percentile top speed by NHL EDGE). Watch whether the trade talk follows him all season.
